title: Performance of ionic liquid–based quasi‐solid‐state hybrid battery supercapacitor fabricated with porous carbon capacitive cathode and proton battery anode

authors.name: Manoj K. Singh

abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>The present paper reports preparation, characterization, and application of proton‐conducting ionic liquid–based gel polymer electrolyte (ILGPE) obtained by immobilizing liquid electrolyte solution (0.3M NH<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>Tf in EMIMTf) to the polymer PVdF‐HFP. These ILGPE offer excellent ionic conductivity ~1.30 × 10<jats:sup>−2</jats:sup> S/cm at room temperature and used as separator membrane in the hybrid BatCap. DSC study confirms glass transitions and melting temperatures (<jats:italic>T</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>g</jats:italic></jats:sub>'s and <jats:italic>T</jats:italic><jats:sub><jats:italic>m</jats:italic></jats:sub>'s) of PVdF‐HFP/EMIMTF/NH<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>Tf decrease with increasing content of liquid electrolyte to the host polymer matrix PVdF‐HFP which, in turn, is responsible for increasing flexibility of membranes. Ionic transport number measurements (<jats:italic>t</jats:italic><jats:sub>ion</jats:sub> ~0.99, <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="graphic/est2310-math-0001.png" xlink:title="urn:x-wiley:25784862:media:est2310:est2310-math-0001"/> ~0.27) reveal that ions are the principal charge carriers in the present electrolyte system. The linear sweep voltammetry analysis shows the electrochemical stability window (ESW) of ILGPE film “PVdF‐HFP/EMIMTf/NH<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>Tf” is ~3.35 V. Two different hybrid BatCap cells are prepared with activated carbon and MWCNTs as a capacitive electrode (cathode) and ZnSO<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>·7H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O battery anode. The performance of the BatCaps is estimated using cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic charge‐discharge techniques. The discharge capacity was observed ~2.4 and 17.2 mAh/g for Cell#1 and Cell#2, respectively, at the current load of 0.5 mA/cm<jats:sup>2</jats:sup>. After the initial fading (~20%), BatCap cells show stable performance up to 100 cycles.</jats:p>
